context: area: src/features/workflows/workflowManager.ts — COMPANION_WORKFLOW is a fixed 5-step list
area: src/features/spec-viewer/specViewerProvider.ts + specExplorerProvider.ts resolve steps via getWorkflow/resolveWorkflow
area: speckit-extension/scripts/pipeline-graph.py already exposes name/after/inSequence/own/artifacts per step
constraint: built-in workflow names are reserved; a custom workflow may not shadow them
constraint: one shared builder produces every pick-surface workflow list
constraint: viewer state derives from recorded run history, not file presence
intent: Make the spec viewer draw the Companion pipeline a project actually runs, so a step added from the builder appears in the rail with its own tab and forward action.
expectations: Do not write a speckit.customWorkflows entry to make an added step visible
Do not copy the Companion pipeline into a user-defined workflow
Do not change how the builder writes a step directory
Placing a step behind another added step is out of scope
Do not introduce file-presence as evidence a step completed
approach: Read the project's own step directories in TypeScript and splice the placed ones into the Companion pipeline at one shared resolver, so the rail, sidebar, footer and timing all draw the pipeline the project actually runs. COMPANION_WORKFLOW stays the shipped literal; the splice happens above it. Three existing guards that key on a fixed step list are widened so an added step is journaled and never falls back to file-presence progression.

decisions.decision: Read .specify/companion/nodes/*/ directly with fs in TypeScript
decisions.why: The rail resolves on every spec open and every sidebar row; spawning python3 there would put a process launch behind each refresh and would fail to draw on a machine without Python, which FR-007 forbids. The viewer needs three fields per step, not the whole graph.
decisions.rejected: Shell out to pipeline-graph.py and reuse its steps[].after / inSequence / artifacts

decisions.decision: Splice above COMPANION_WORKFLOW rather than mutating it
decisions.why: It is read as a module constant by buildWorkflowChoices, customWorkflowProgress and the viewer tests; mutating it would make all of those workspace-dependent and break SC-003.
decisions.rejected: Rebuild COMPANION_WORKFLOW from the workspace at activation

decisions.decision: No cache on the directory read
decisions.why: The common case is one readdir that ENOENTs; a cache would need a watcher and a disposal lifecycle to save unmeasured work.
decisions.rejected: Cache per workspace root invalidated by the existing .specify watcher — held in reserve if the sidebar gets slow

decisions.decision: Detect a built-in pipeline by its command family (speckit.companion.*)
decisions.why: A spliced Companion pipeline no longer matches the literal signature, so customWorkflowProgress would switch it to file-presence progression — exactly what FR-009 rules out. The command family is what actually distinguishes a pipeline that captures.
decisions.rejected: Compare the sequence with project steps removed, or add an explicit isBuiltin flag to WorkflowConfig

decisions.decision: Derive the lifecycle-step predicate from the resolved pipeline
decisions.why: The two hardcoded sets answer a name question when the real one is whether the step records anything; a name-based set would leave an added step with a completion that never began.
decisions.rejected: Add each project step name to both sets at read time

decisions.decision: Recognise a built-in pipeline by its command family (every step dispatching speckit.companion.*) in addition to the exact shipped sequence
decisions.why: A spliced Companion pipeline no longer matches the shipped sequence, and the companion name is reserved so no user workflow can claim that prefix
decisions.rejected: Rebuilding the expected sequence per workspace, which would have re-read the step directory inside the classifier

decisions.decision: shouldRecordStepStart gates on pipeline membership, not untimed, and a speckit. command prefix, with clarify and analyze kept as off-pipeline exceptions
decisions.why: Pipeline membership alone would have stopped journaling clarify and analyze, which are side commands in no pipeline; the command prefix is what keeps a user-workflow step from recording
decisions.rejected: Pure pipeline membership as the contract described, which silently dropped the two side commands

decisions.decision: Badge every step in the resolved pipeline, not only the lifecycle names
decisions.why: deriveStepBadges iterated the fixed STEP_NAMES set, so an added step drew a blank rail mark even once the resolver placed it
decisions.rejected: Leaving the badge map alone, which would have shipped a visible step with no state

decisions.decision: Resolve the pipeline once at the top of executeWorkflowStep and use it for progress, per-step model/effort and terminal tracking
decisions.why: Those three all read the un-spliced normalized.steps, so an added step would have been drawn but not progressed
decisions.rejected: Swapping only the three LIFECYCLE_STEPS checks the task named

plan.summary: Plan, research, data model and contract written: read the project step directory in TS, splice into Companion at one shared resolver, widen three guards that key on a fixed step list.
plan.key_finding: Splicing the Companion pipeline trips two existing guards nobody would look for — customWorkflowProgress would reclassify it as user-defined and start inferring completion from files on disk (violating FR-009), and the two hardcoded lifecycle-step sets would refuse to write a start for the added step.
